findings.title: Duplicate self.downsize definition silently overrides the 4-argument version
findings.body: The file now defines `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and then immediately redefines `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. In Ruby the second definition wins, so the 4-positional-argument version is dead code. Any existing caller that invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 3..4)` — worse, a call with width and height will be treated as `dimensions = width` and `opts = height`, producing garbage ImageMagick dimensions instead of an error. Either remove the old overload or keep only one signature.

findings.title: Client-side upload size check hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously enforced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; this PR replaces it with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB. If an admin sets a smaller limit (e.g. 2MB images, or lower attachment limits), users get no client-side warning and only learn about the failure after the upload round-trips to the server; if they set a larger limit, the client still blocks at 10MB. The same hardcoding was applied to the 413 handler at line 246. The site setting lookup should be kept (and the error message will then report the correct limit).

findings.title: API URL downloads now hard-capped at 10MB regardless of configured limits
findings.body: The download limit for API-provided URLs was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Admins who raise max_image_size_kb above 10MB still cannot pull larger images via the API (download returns nil and the upload fails with a confusing error), and the magic number can drift from the client-side and server-side limits. The downsize logic added below makes the original intent (download up to some cap, then shrink) work, but the cap should be a setting-derived value, e.g. a multiple of max_image_size_kb, not a literal.

findings.title: Downsize loop keeps shrinking in place and gives up silently on failure
findings.body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times without checking the return value. Two problems: (1) each iteration recompresses the already-downsized file at 80% of the previous dimensions, so an image that needs more than one pass ends up drastically smaller and more degraded than necessary (0.8^5 ≈ 33% of original dimensions) rather than being resized once to a target that fits the byte limit; (2) if `downsize` fails (e.g. ImageMagick error on a corrupt/unsupported file), it returns false, the file size never changes, the loop burns through all 5 attempts running convert 5 times for nothing, and the oversized file is passed on to `Upload.create_for` anyway. The return value should break the loop, and a single computed resize (or at least checking progress between iterations) would avoid the compounding quality loss.

findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing reuses thumbnail resize-fit instructions and drops animation framing
findings.body: For animated GIFs the `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` path routes to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which just delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` (gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`). Passing a percentage to gifsicle's --resize-fit is not valid geometry (it expects WxH), so animated GIFs over the size limit will fail to downsize (convert returns non-zero, loop no-ops) and the upload then fails validation. Additionally, tying upload downsizing of animations to the `allow_animated_thumbnails` setting conflates two unrelated features — a site that disables animated thumbnails still wants animated originals downsized.
